correctness.rationale: For ideal qubit H=ħΩσ_x and projective survival tests, exact conditional probability is ∏cos²(b_m X_j). Pareto tail gives v(b)=E sin²(bX)=α b^α ∫_b∞sin²(z)z^(−1−α)dz with asymptotics Kα b^α (α<2), 2b² log(1/b) (α=2), and b² α/(α−2) (α>2). At b_m=c m^(−1/α), the point-process Laplace functional yields a strictly positive nonconstant random limit ∏_{PPP}cos² z with intensity αc^α z^(−1−α)dz; the product is well-defined since zero-neighborhood quadratic loss is summable, and PPP a.s. avoids cosine zeros. Integer moments determine a [0,1] law. First and second exact moments are exp(−c^α Kα) and exp(−c^α Kα(1+2^(α−2))) with Kα=π2^(α−2)/(Γα sin(πα/2)), yielding positive variance for α<2. At α=2 a truncated second-moment concentration gives e^(−c²) with scale (m log m)^−1/2; at α>2 WLLN yields e^(−c² α/(α−2)) with m^−1/2. Sharp small/large normalization follows from E P_m=(1−v(b_m))^m and endpoint Markov; independent finite numerical integration checked α1 Fourier constant and c=.7 moments, not an infinite proof. No fixed total time assertion.

originality.rationale: Earlier randomized quantum-Zeno work supplies conditional cosine-product dynamics and large-deviation settings. Gherardini et al. fixed waiting-time distribution and their power-tail example treats finite second moments, while Shushin analyses stochastic-time renewal/elapsed-time phenomena. The precise triangular array across α=2, PPP nonselfaveraging law, exact Mellin/variance constants, and sharp scale trichotomy are distinct statement-level results; they are not new general Poisson process mathematics.
